report_name: FBI Warns of Sophisticated OAuth Consent Phishing Campaign

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: Attackers send a direct message containing a lure with a link to a malicious OAuth consent screen.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: The core of the attack involves tricking a user into granting consent to a malicious application, which allows the attacker to steal an application access token for persistent, programmatic access to the user's cloud account data.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing via Service
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors initiate contact with targets by sending a direct message via a commercial messaging application, impersonating credible figures to build trust.

campaigns.name: OAuth Consent Phishing Campaign
campaigns.description: An ongoing phishing campaign active since late 2025 that uses OAuth consent phishing to gain persistent access to the cloud accounts of high-profile individuals.
campaigns.objective: Gain persistent, password-independent access to the cloud accounts of prominent individuals for data theft and espionage.

identities.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
identities.description: Issued a Public Service Announcement (PSA) through its Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) to warn about the OAuth consent phishing campaign.

identities.name: Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
identities.description: The FBI's center for receiving and processing cyber crime complaints, which co-issued the warning.

identities.name: Microsoft
identities.description: One of the cloud service providers whose OAuth framework is being abused by attackers in the campaign.

identities.name: Google
identities.description: One of the cloud service providers whose OAuth framework is being abused by attackers in the campaign.

identities.name: High-profile individuals
identities.description: The primary targets of the OAuth consent phishing campaign, including their families and associates.

identities.name: Government officials
identities.description: A specific class of high-profile individuals targeted for potential espionage.

identities.name: Journalists
identities.description: A specific class of high-profile individuals targeted for potential espionage.

infrastructure.name: Malicious OAuth Application
infrastructure.description: A third-party application controlled by the attacker, which victims are tricked into granting permissions to, enabling account access via stolen tokens.

infrastructure.name: OAuth Authorization Endpoint
infrastructure.description: Legitimate OAuth consent screens from major cloud providers (like Microsoft or Google) that are used as part of the phishing lure to make the permission grant request seem authentic.

indicators.name: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth Consent Auditing
indicators.pattern:
title: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth Application Consent
id: 2795c6f0-a8b1-4d3e-8f9a-1c2d3e4f5a6b
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects when a user grants consent to an application in Microsoft Entra ID. This should be investigated for unfamiliar or newly created applications, as it is a key step in OAuth consent phishing.
references:
  - https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-alert-oauth-consent-phishing-campaign/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-02
tags:
  - attack.t1528
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection:
    OperationName: 'Consent to application'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Monitors Microsoft Entra ID audit logs for 'Consent to application' events, which can indicate OAuth consent phishing. Unfamiliar or newly created applications should be investigated.

indicators.name: Google Workspace OAuth Permission Grant Auditing
indicators.pattern:
title: Google Workspace OAuth Application Permission Grant
id: 8b1a2c3d-4e5f-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects when a user grants application permissions in Google Workspace. This should be investigated for apps with high-risk permissions, as it is a key step in OAuth consent phishing.
references:
  - https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-alert-oauth-consent-phishing-campaign/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-02
tags:
  - attack.t1528
level: medium
logsource:
  product: gcp
  service: gcp.audit
detection:
  selection:
    gcp.audit.method_name: 'google.admin.AdminService.apps.activities.list'
    gcp.audit.resource.service: 'admin.googleapis.com'
    json.events.name: 'GRANT_APPLICATION_PERMISSION'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Monitors Google Workspace admin audit logs for 'GRANT_APPLICATION_PERMISSION' events. Apps granted high-risk permissions should be scrutinized.

indicators.name: Suspicious OAuth Application Permissions
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious High-Risk OAuth Permissions Granted
id: 5a6b7c8d-9e0f-4a1b-2c3d-4e5f6a7b8c9d
status: experimental
description: >
  Identifies when applications are granted high-risk OAuth permissions such as 'Mail.ReadWrite', 'Files.ReadWrite.All', or 'offline_access'. Such permissions are commonly sought in consent phishing attacks.
references:
  - https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-alert-oauth-consent-phishing-campaign/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-02
tags:
  - attack.t1528
level: high
logsource:
  category: cloud
detection:
  keywords:
    - 'Mail.ReadWrite'
    - 'Files.ReadWrite.All'
    - 'offline_access'
  condition: keywords
indicators.description: Detects the granting of broad, high-risk permissions like 'Mail.ReadWrite', 'Files.ReadWrite.All', or 'offline_access' to applications, which is a common indicator of consent phishing.

indicators.name: OAuth Consent Phishing Authorization Endpoint
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Microsoft OAuth Authorization Endpoint Access
id: 9f8e7d6c-5b4a-4c3d-2e1f-0a9b8c7d6e5f
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects network traffic to the legitimate Microsoft OAuth authorization endpoint. While the endpoint itself is legitimate, a high volume of requests or requests from unusual sources could indicate a consent phishing campaign.
references:
  - https://cyberscoop.com/fbi-alert-oauth-consent-phishing-campaign/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-02
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
level: informational
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri: 'https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects traffic to the legitimate Microsoft OAuth authorization endpoint, which is used in consent phishing attacks. The key malicious indicator is the client_id parameter within the URL, which identifies the attacker's application.
